revision_reason: Re-assessment after architect revision 2 addressed all 5 plan reviewer feedback items. This revision confirms resolution of the original issues and identifies 3 remaining gaps not covered by the revised plan.
title: Risk Assessment: Add interactive pre-refine step to SDLC pipeline
summary: The proposed PRE_REFINE phase implementation (Approach A) is architecturally sound. The architect's revision 2 correctly addresses all 5 original review feedback items (gateway phase infrastructure, dag_visualizer, sdlc_hitl _get_draft_path, pipeline starting phase mechanism, backward compatibility contradiction). However, 3 remaining gaps exist: (1) gateway/gateway.py:3176 VALID_PIPELINE_PHASES frozenset, (2) shared/egg_contracts/agent_roles.py _PHASE_ROLES/_PHASE_REVIEWERS dicts, and (3) no cross-file synchronization tests. All identified risks are mitigable. Overall risk level: MEDIUM. Verdict: APPROVE WITH CONDITIONS.

risk_assessment.overall_verdict: Proceed with Approach A. The approach is architecturally sound — modeling pre-refine as a first-class phase provides clean state semantics, SSE observability, and restart capability. The architect's revision 2 substantially addresses the review feedback. Three remaining gaps (detailed below) are straightforward additions to Phase 1. All risks are mitigable with disciplined execution.
risk_assessment.confidence: High — based on source code analysis of all affected files across gateway, orchestrator, shared contracts, and sandbox packages

review_feedback_resolution_assessment.summary: All 5 original review feedback items are correctly resolved in the architect's revision 2.

feedback_1_gateway_phase_infrastructure.assessment: New tasks TASK-1-7 (gateway/phase_filter.py enum + PhasePermissions + PhaseFileRestriction) and TASK-1-8 (gateway/phase_transition.py VALID_TRANSITIONS) correctly address the gateway phase infrastructure. The specified PRE_REFINE permissions are appropriately minimal. The incorrect backward compatibility claim has been removed.

feedback_2_dag_visualizer.assessment: New task TASK-1-9 correctly adds PRE_REFINE to PHASE_ORDER (index 0) and PHASE_NAMES. All usage sites (DAG rendering line 372, compact status line 530, progress bar line 562, report generation line 636) iterate PHASE_ORDER, so the addition is sufficient.
feedback_2_dag_visualizer.residual_risk: LOW — but see NEW-GAP-2 regarding _PHASE_ROLES dependency

feedback_3_sdlc_hitl_get_draft_path.assessment: New task TASK-3-5 correctly adds explicit pre_refine branch to sdlc_hitl.py:_get_draft_path(). The investigation correctly identified the generic fallback would produce the wrong filename.

feedback_4_pipeline_starting_phase.assessment: TASK-2-1 updated to specify the mechanism: _run_pipeline() checks PipelineConfig.skip_pre_refine at startup, before the phase loop. If false AND no existing requirements document, sets current_phase to PRE_REFINE. Pipeline model default stays REFINE. This is the cleanest approach — preserves backward compatibility, co-locates logic, handles re-runs.
feedback_4_pipeline_starting_phase.residual_risk: MEDIUM — see RISK-4 regarding placement in the large _run_pipeline() function

feedback_5_backward_compatibility.assessment: PipelineConfig.skip_pre_refine defaults to true (opt-in model). CLI interactive mode explicitly sets false. This correctly decouples config default (backward-compatible) from CLI default (user-friendly).

new_gaps_in_revised_plan.title: gateway/gateway.py:3176 VALID_PIPELINE_PHASES frozenset not in any task
new_gaps_in_revised_plan.description: gateway/gateway.py:3176 defines VALID_PIPELINE_PHASES = frozenset({'refine', 'plan', 'implement', 'pr'}). This hardcoded set is used at lines 2721 and 3207 to validate phase values in session_register() and session_update_phase(). Without adding 'pre_refine', the gateway rejects ALL operations referencing the pre_refine phase with 'Invalid phase' errors. This is a complete pipeline blockage — no container can register for the pre_refine phase and no phase update to pre_refine can succeed.
new_gaps_in_revised_plan.recommendation: Add 'pre_refine' to the VALID_PIPELINE_PHASES frozenset in Phase 1 alongside TASK-1-7 and TASK-1-8. One-line change but its omission blocks the entire feature.

new_gaps_in_revised_plan.title: shared/egg_contracts/agent_roles.py _PHASE_ROLES and _PHASE_REVIEWERS not in any task
new_gaps_in_revised_plan.description: agent_roles.py:763 defines _PHASE_ROLES dict and line 769 defines _PHASE_REVIEWERS dict. get_roles_for_phase() at line 800 raises ValueError if phase not in _PHASE_ROLES. This function is called by dag_visualizer.py:169 during DAG rendering. If PRE_REFINE is added to PHASE_ORDER (TASK-1-9) but not to _PHASE_ROLES, DAG visualization crashes with ValueError for ALL pipelines (not just PRE_REFINE ones), because the DAG renders all phases. The _run_pipeline() function at ~line 4229 also selects agent roles based on phase and ~line 4382 looks up reviewers.
new_gaps_in_revised_plan.recommendation: Add _PHASE_ROLES['pre_refine'] = [] (no agents — human-driven phase) and _PHASE_REVIEWERS['pre_refine'] = [] (no review cycle) in Phase 1. Must be done BEFORE or WITH the PHASE_ORDER change in TASK-1-9, otherwise DAG rendering crashes.

new_gaps_in_revised_plan.title: No cross-file synchronization tests proposed
new_gaps_in_revised_plan.description: PipelinePhase exists in 3 enum copies, transitions in 3 maps, permissions in 2 defaults + 1 JSON, roles in 2 dicts, visualization in 2 structures. No existing test validates these are in sync. The plan's Phase 5 does not include consistency tests. This is a systemic risk: the same gap-finding exercise will be needed for any future phase addition.
new_gaps_in_revised_plan.recommendation: Add to Phase 5: a test asserting all PipelinePhase enum copies have identical members, all phases have entries in _PHASE_ROLES, _PHASE_REVIEWERS, _DEFAULT_PHASE_CONFIGS, PHASE_ORDER, PHASE_NAMES, and both transition maps. This prevents regression.

risks.title: Triple-enum synchronization failure
risks.description: PipelinePhase is defined in 3 files (orchestrator/models.py:15, shared/egg_contracts/models.py:34, gateway/phase_filter.py:28) with explicit 'must be kept in sync' comments. If any copy is missed, phase deserialization and comparison fail. The gateway copy is most critical since it controls enforcement.
risks.plan_status: COVERED — The revised plan's Phase 1 includes all three locations (TASK-1-1/1-2 for orchestrator/shared, TASK-1-7 for gateway).
risks.mitigation: Update all three in a SINGLE commit. Add a cross-file sync test (NEW-GAP-3).
risks.rollback: Revert the commit. Purely additive change.

risks.title: Gateway blocks PRE_REFINE via VALID_PIPELINE_PHASES frozenset
risks.description: gateway/gateway.py:3176 VALID_PIPELINE_PHASES is a hardcoded frozenset used at lines 2721 and 3207. Not in the revised plan. Without 'pre_refine', gateway rejects all PRE_REFINE operations.
risks.mitigation: Add 'pre_refine' to the frozenset. One-line change in Phase 1.

risks.title: DAG visualization crash from missing _PHASE_ROLES entry
risks.description: get_roles_for_phase('pre_refine') raises ValueError at agent_roles.py:801-802. Called by dag_visualizer.py:169 for ALL phases during DAG rendering. Crashes visualization for every pipeline, not just PRE_REFINE ones.
risks.mitigation: Add _PHASE_ROLES['pre_refine'] = [] and _PHASE_REVIEWERS['pre_refine'] = []. Must precede or accompany TASK-1-9.
risks.rollback: Remove entries or remove PRE_REFINE from PHASE_ORDER.

risks.title: PRE_REFINE breaks standard phase execution model in _run_pipeline()
risks.description: All existing phases follow: spawn container -> wait -> read artifacts -> review -> HITL gate. PRE_REFINE breaks this: immediately pause for human interaction, no container. _run_pipeline() has 7+ phase-conditional branches: _HITL_GATE_PHASES (line 3231), multi-agent detection (~4093), agent role selection (~4229), checker spawning (~4295), reviewer lookup (~4382), contract population (~4664), HITL gate (~4686). Each must either handle PRE_REFINE or be skipped via early-exit.
risks.plan_status: PARTIALLY COVERED — TASK-2-1 describes PRE_REFINE handling but does not prescribe the early-exit pattern.
risks.mitigation: Use early-exit pattern: at top of phase loop iteration, check if current_phase == PRE_REFINE, handle it entirely (set AWAITING_HUMAN, queue decision), then 'continue'. This prevents PRE_REFINE logic from scattering across all 7 branches.

risks.title: Fail-open security if PRE_REFINE permissions not defined in both locations
risks.description: Phase permissions are defined in two places: .egg/phase-permissions.json (loaded dynamically, unknown phases silently skipped) and gateway/phase_filter.py hardcoded defaults (fallback if JSON missing). If PRE_REFINE is absent from both, the gateway defaults to permissive behavior. Pre-refine should be the most restrictive phase.
risks.plan_status: COVERED — TASK-1-4 covers JSON, TASK-1-7 covers hardcoded defaults.
risks.mitigation: Ensure BOTH are updated. PRE_REFINE permissions: only .egg-state/drafts/*requirements* writes, no code files, no PR operations.
risks.rollback: Remove entries. Gateway falls back to permissive but VALID_PIPELINE_PHASES prevents PRE_REFINE use entirely.

risks.title: Dual _get_draft_path() divergence
risks.description: Two independent _get_draft_path() implementations must produce identical paths: orchestrator/routes/pipelines.py:1037 (server) and sandbox/egg_lib/sdlc_hitl.py:27 (CLI client). The sdlc_hitl.py generic fallback produces '{prefix}-pre_refine.md' instead of '{prefix}-requirements.md'.
risks.plan_status: COVERED — TASK-2-2 (orchestrator) and TASK-3-5 (sdlc_hitl.py) both add explicit pre_refine branches.
risks.mitigation: Both must map pre_refine to '{prefix}-requirements.md'. Add a test asserting both functions produce the same path for each phase.
risks.rollback: Remove branches. Generic fallback produces non-standard path but doesn't crash.

risks.title: Interactive Claude session crash loses conversation context
risks.description: If the Claude session crashes mid-conversation, the requirements document may have partial content (if incremental writes are used) but conversation context is lost. The human must restart the conversation. Pipeline stays in AWAITING_HUMAN so it's resumable, but the Claude session state is not persisted.
risks.plan_status: PARTIALLY COVERED — Plan specifies incremental writes but does not specify resume-from-partial-draft behavior.
risks.mitigation: handle_pre_refine() should detect existing partial requirements draft on resume and offer to continue. The system prompt for the resumed session should include the partial draft as context.
risks.rollback: Pipeline stays in AWAITING_HUMAN. User can cancel or restart.

risks.title: Transition map divergence between gateway and orchestrator
risks.description: Phase transitions validated in gateway/phase_transition.py (enforcement) and orchestrator/routes/phases.py (logic). If PRE_REFINE -> [REFINE] is in one but not the other, pipelines get stuck (gateway rejects) or bypass validation (orchestrator skips check).
risks.plan_status: COVERED — TASK-1-3 (orchestrator) and TASK-1-8 (gateway) both add PRE_REFINE -> [REFINE].
risks.mitigation: Update both in the same commit. Add cross-validation test (NEW-GAP-3).

risks.title: Existing test assertions break on new enum value
risks.description: Tests in test_phase_transition.py, test_dag_visualizer.py, and test_phase_defaults.py contain hardcoded phase count assertions. Adding PRE_REFINE will break these. This is expected and healthy — the failures serve as a checklist.
risks.plan_status: COVERED in Phase 5 but should be partially done in Phase 1.
risks.mitigation: Fix basic assertion updates (phase counts, enum iteration) in Phase 1 alongside enum changes. Phase 5 focuses on NEW PRE_REFINE behavior tests.

risks.title: Issue body replacement may affect downstream automation
risks.description: In issue mode, approved requirements replace the GitHub issue body. Original preserved in <details> section. Tools parsing issue body (e.g., JIRA sync) may not handle the format change. The refine agent reads the issue body, which after pre-refine will be the requirements document — this is the intended behavior.
risks.plan_status: COVERED — TASK-4-1 specifies the <details> preservation approach.
risks.mitigation: Standard GitHub practice. Original recoverable from <details> section and GitHub edit history.
risks.rollback: Restore original body via gh issue edit.

risks.title: Requirements document quality not validated
risks.description: The requirements document is free-form markdown. If poorly structured or excessively long, the refine agent's prompt may exceed context limits or produce degraded analysis. No schema validation exists.
risks.plan_status: PARTIALLY COVERED — System prompt guides structure but no validation.
risks.mitigation: Claude's system prompt guides toward structured format (problem statement, requirements, constraints, acceptance criteria). Consider truncating very long documents in _build_phase_prompt() with a warning. Refine agent already handles arbitrary issue body text.
risks.rollback: N/A — refine falls back to original issue body if no requirements document exists.

risks.title: Headless/CI callers silently skip pre-refine with no indication
risks.description: With skip_pre_refine defaulting to true, all headless/CI callers skip pre-refine silently. No log, SSE event, or status indicator that it was available but skipped.
risks.mitigation: Add a log message when skip_pre_refine=true: 'Pre-refine phase skipped (skip_pre_refine=true)'. Nice-to-have, not blocking.

areas_requiring_human_review.reason: Architectural decision about code placement in the most complex file in the codebase (~5100 lines). The early-exit pattern is recommended to prevent scattered conditionals across 7+ phase-specific branches.
Security-critical configuration. PRE_REFINE should be the most restrictive phase. Both .egg/phase-permissions.json and gateway/phase_filter.py defaults must define correct restrictions.
UX-critical. The quality of the pre-refine step depends on Claude's system prompt. Should guide conversation toward clear requirements without being rigid.

rollback_plan.strategy: Additive changes across 5 ordered phases. Rollback at any phase boundary by reverting all commits from that phase.
rollback_plan.soft_disable: Set skip_pre_refine=true in all pipeline creation paths. No code changes needed. PRE_REFINE code remains but is never activated.
rollback_plan.full_revert: Remove PRE_REFINE from all enum definitions, transition maps, permissions, and conditional logic. Safe because PRE_REFINE is new — no existing data depends on it.
rollback_plan.data_migration: None required. Existing pipelines never enter PRE_REFINE. Pipelines in PRE_REFINE during rollback can be manually advanced via egg-orch phase advance.

security_assessment.overall: LOW risk. PRE_REFINE is designed as the most restrictive phase. Main concern is correct permission configuration (RISK-5, covered by plan).

items.concern: Claude session could access repository files
items.status: MITIGATED by design (TD-7, no codebase access)

items.concern: Issue body replacement used for injection
items.status: ACCEPTABLE — document consumed as plain text

performance_assessment.overall: NEGLIGIBLE impact. One additional optional phase, no changes to existing phase execution.
items: DAG rendering: +1 iteration in PHASE_ORDER loops — negligible
Pipeline startup: +1 conditional check for skip_pre_refine — negligible
Progress bar: denominator changes from 4 to 5 phases — cosmetic only

conditions_for_approval: Phase 1 must include gateway/gateway.py VALID_PIPELINE_PHASES update (NEW-GAP-1)
Phase 1 must include agent_roles.py _PHASE_ROLES and _PHASE_REVIEWERS entries (NEW-GAP-2)
Phase 5 should include cross-file synchronization tests (NEW-GAP-3)
Human must review phase-permissions.json entry and gateway enforcement updates
Full test suite must pass after Phase 1 before proceeding to Phase 2
